$comment: Declares every PRIVATE corpus input this repository's tests depend on. Contains NO corpus
content -- only names, relative paths, purpose, and which tests require them.
Why this file exists: the real-language inputs under samples/data/ are intentionally
untracked, and many corpus-dependent tests are #[ignore]d with a skip-if-absent guard. That
combination is a false-success path -- a worktree can report that it ran the corpus suite
while testing no corpus data at all. Observed: a fresh agent worktree has no samples/data/,
so every such test returned success having measured nothing.
Contract: `pg.ps1 -Mode corpus-test` validates every required path in this manifest BEFORE
cargo starts and refuses to run if any is missing. It also sets PANGLOSS_CORPUS_REQUIRED=1,
which flips the Rust helpers in pg_conformance_fixtures::corpus from skip-if-absent to panic-
if-absent. Ordinary fixture-independent test runs are unaffected.
Keep `requiring_tests` accurate: it is how a reader finds what breaks when a corpus goes
missing, and the manifest-validation test checks the shape of every entry.

corpora.purpose: Template-less standalone-rule morphotactics with MPR-gated nasal substitution. The reference grammar for proposer recall on the gated compile path, and the only real grammar whose backend candidates currently reach full-HC confirmation.

word_list.notes: No header. Two known non-representative lines documented in docs/fst-plan/corpus-word-list-hazards.md: line 100 'meⁿ' is alphabet-valid (segment char29) but is a bound meN- prefix fragment with no attached root, so it always analyzes as ok/no-parse ('-'); line 119 'write-CONTpijit' is gloss-template contamination (uppercase Latin letters + an English word + a gloss abbreviation) that contains characters outside the char table and is always batch status SKIPPED.

corpora.purpose: Large-lexicon templated grammar (255k+ lexc lines). Drives emit/compile throughput and the propose-then-confirm perf track.

word_list.notes: No header, but the char table (samples/data/sena-hc.xml) defines no hyphen segment or boundary, so all ~73 hyphenated reduplication entries (e.g. 'ampfaka-mpfaca') are guaranteed batch status SKIPPED, not a recall failure. A handful of lines are outright non-word contamination and should be excluded from any recall measurement: 'require' (English), 'neg-2psing'/'neg-3p'/'h-u-dadya'/'h-a-da-dya' (interlinear-gloss/morpheme-break debris), 'v-front' and 'det-suffix' (metalinguistic labels), 'lox2' (stray digit). A few more (e.g. 'fátima', 'subtítulo', 'cabeça', 'secondário') are Portuguese loan/proper-noun spellings using accented characters (á/í/ç) also absent from the char table. Full accounting in docs/fst-plan/corpus-word-list-hazards.md.

corpora.purpose: Templatic root-and-pattern interdigitation with AffixTemplate morphotactics. The grammar whose productive morphology lives in the composite-emission and structural-composite subtrees that build_controllable does not build.

word_list.notes: Lines 1-4 are an English-gloss header ('break','pay','pfv','want'), not Ethiopic surface words; a naive head -N slice reads these as unanalyzable words and presents as a recall failure (the motivating bug for docs/fst-plan/corpus-word-list-hazards.md). Real words start at line 5. Separately, 17 word lines beyond the header (e.g. lines 63-65, 71-75, 91, 105, 355, 502, 512, 601, 604, 615, 627) use Ethiopic letter variants (ሕ ሐ ሥ ሦ ሃ ዓ ፀ) that are absent from the grammar's CharacterDefinitionTable and are therefore also guaranteed batch status SKIPPED. This corpus is also SLOW: several individual words (e.g. lines 5, 12, 17, 29-32) take multiple seconds to confirm and can make even a 40-word sample exceed a naive process timeout; always pass --word-timeout-ms to `pangloss batch` when sampling it.

corpora.purpose: Deep truncation chain with a 24-level derivation and many zero-width truncation mrules. The enumeration-explosion and compose-budget stress case; imported from fwdata/JSON rather than HC XML.

word_list.notes: No header, but the phonology's phonemes/boundaryMarkers (samples/data/aweti.json) define no hyphen or space, so lines containing either (e.g. 'itywytu-put', 'waráju-puza', 'kaminuʼat-puza', 'ị- tyᴾ', 'awytyza ʼytoto') are guaranteed batch status SKIPPED. Line 147 is a stray 'µ' (micro sign) with no linguistic content; line 175 'wejmopáb' ends in a bare 'b', a phoneme this inventory does not define outside its ejective-marked forms. Separately and more importantly: this grammar has known pathological words (docs/fst-plan/corpus-word-list-hazards.md; matches the memory'd apply_up explosion, e.g. 'tomoʼatu') that hang and grow RSS into the tens of GB under the default HC-oracle batch path -- confirmed to reach ~30GB before being killed. Sampling MUST pass both --word-timeout-ms and --threads=1 to `pangloss batch`; the default --threads=20 multiplies several such words' memory blowups concurrently and can exhaust host memory, which is an operational hazard to the whole machine, not just this run.
